en.title: The Book of Dao · Chapter Twenty-three · Holding the One
en.原文:
曲則金
枉則定
洼則盈
敝則新
少則得
多則惑

是以聲人執一以為天下牧

不自視故章不自見也故明
不自伐故有功
弗矜故能長

夫唯不爭
故莫能與之爭

古之所胃曲全者幾語才
誠金歸之

不自見故明，不自是故彰，不自伐故有功，不自矜故長。夫唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。古之所謂曲則全者，豈虛言哉！誠全而歸之。
en.校記:
The text follows Manuscript A (MS A); the lines 不自視故章不自見也故明 and 古之所胃曲全者幾語才, damaged in MS A, are supplied from Manuscript B (MS B). Graphs are those outside the brackets in the *Changsha Mawangdui Han mu jianbo jicheng* (2014; hereafter *Jicheng*).

- 曲則金: Follows MS A. 金 is a scribal error for 全 "whole", which the *Jicheng* corrects to 〈全〉; MS B reads 曲則全, as does Wang Bi.
- 枉則定: Follows MS A, with 定 read as 正 "straight"; MS B reads 汪則正, with 汪 read as 枉 "crooked". Wang Bi has 枉則直.
- 洼則盈 / 敝則新: Follows MS A, with 洼 read as 窪 "hollow". MS B writes 敝 as 𧝬 (敝 over 衣), as the plates, the 1980 edition and Gao Ming's transcription all show.
- 是以聲人執一以為天下牧: Follows MS A, with 聲 read as 聖 "sage"; MS B writes 聖 as 𦔻 (耳 beside 口). Wang Bi has 是以聖人抱一為天下式, with 抱 "embrace" for 執 "hold" and 式 "pattern" for 牧 "shepherd".
- 不自視故章不自見也故明: Follows MS B. MS A reads 不【自】視故明，不自見故章; MS B reads 不自視故章，不自見也故明. The two manuscripts thus exchange 明 and 章, and MS B has 也 in the second line. Since 自 is lost in MS A, both clauses follow MS B, so that 明 and 章 are not mixed. The *Jicheng* reads 視 as 示 "to display" and 章 as 彰 "to be manifest". Wang Bi has 不自見故明，不自是故彰.
- 弗矜故能長: The manuscripts agree; Wang Bi has 不自矜故長.
- 故莫能與之爭: The manuscripts agree; Wang Bi has 故天下莫能與之爭.
- 古之所胃曲全者幾語才: Lost after 古 in MS A; the line follows MS B. MS A's 語 was read directly in the 1980 edition, but the *Jicheng* finds that the fragment bearing its left side is not the 言 radical, removes it, and reads 唔（語）; the graph above it keeps some traces, and the *Jicheng* withdraws the 1980 restoration 幾 (taken from MS B) in favour of ☐. MS B's 才 is read as 哉. Wang Bi has 古之所謂曲則全者，豈虛言哉. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 51, n. 90)
- 誠金歸之: Follows MS A, where 金 is again an error for 全; MS B reads 誠全歸之. Wang Bi has 誠全而歸之.
en.疏:
杳眇曰：

此章之旨，在陳反向成就之道，而以「執一」為歸宿焉。

夫物之生也，稟道以形，倚道以命。曲則全，枉則正，窪則盈，敝則新，少則得，多則惑——六事一貫，其理則一：盈者必溢，滿者必傾，相反相成，乃道之常則也。曲己以從物，乃得全，此其旨也。曲者非詭，乃屈己以全物；枉者非屈，乃曲而復正。窪以受之，敝以生之，少以守之，多以惑之——聖人觀此，故知矜伐之不可，爭競之無益也。

次言四「不」：不自視故章，不自見也故明，不自伐故有功，弗矜故能長（乙本如此；甲本作「不自視故明，不自見故章」，明、章互易）。帛書之「不自視」，王弼本作「不自是」，字各不同。不自視者，言不眩於所見也，《集成》讀視為示，則不自炫示之謂，義亦相近；王弼之「不自是」，言不執於所是也。二本互見，其義相成，皆聖人輔翼萬物而不自有其功者也。「不自伐故有功」，伐則功折，不伐則功全，正此之謂。弗矜者，不自貴其能也——唯弗矜，故能長，與上善治水「水善利萬物而有靜」義相發明也。

夫唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。此不爭之德，非怯懦也，乃立於不可爭之地。欲爭者必有對手，不爭者天下莫能與之為敵，此道家之上智也。

末云「古之所胃曲全者，幾語才，誠全歸之」。帛書作「幾語才」，言此理豈空言哉；「誠全歸之」，言曲己從物者，終得全歸焉。《中庸》云「誠者，天之道」，老氏以「誠全歸之」言曲全之實，是知儒道本非二途，殊途同歸者也。

王弼本「抱一」與帛書「執一」，執一者執守之也，抱一者涵養之也，辭異而旨同，皆言守道之純、抱德之全，以此事天之道、御人之政也。牧者，養而治之，非威制之，此聖人所以為天下牧者與。
en.疏英:
Yaomiao says:

The point of this chapter is the way of achieving by reversal — and it comes home to "holding the One."

Things are born taking their shape from the Dao, leaning on the Dao for their charge. Bent, then whole; crooked, then straight; hollow, then full; worn, then new; little, then gain; much, then bewilderment — six sayings, one law: the full must spill; the brimming must tip; contraries complete each other — the constant rule of the Dao. Bend yourself to follow things, and wholeness is gained — that is the point. Bending is not scheming: it is bowing the self to make things whole. Crooked is not crushed: it curves and comes back straight. The hollowed receives; the worn gives birth; the little keeps; the much bewilders. The sage, watching this, knows pride and boasting will not do, and contention profits nothing.

Then the four "nots": not self-seeing, and so shown; not self-displaying, and so clear; not self-boasting, and so meritorious; not self-exalting, and so lasting (so manuscript B; manuscript A reads 不自視故明，不自見故章, with 明 and 章 exchanged). The silk text's 不自視 against Wang Bi's 不自是 — the graphs differ. The silk text's "not self-seeing" is not being dazzled by one's own view (the *Jicheng* reads 視 as 示, "not putting oneself on show," a near sense); Wang Bi's "not self-asserting" is not gripping one's own rightness. The two texts face each other, and the senses complete one another — all saying the sage wings the ten thousand things along without claiming the work. "Not self-boasting, and so meritorious": boast, and the merit breaks; boast not, and the merit is whole — just this. Not self-exalting is not prizing one's own ability — only so, lasting: one light with "water benefits the ten thousand things and keeps still."

Only because he does not contend, no one in all-under-heaven can contend with him. This De of not contending is no timidity: it is standing on ground where contention cannot reach. To contend there must be an opposite party; he who does not contend has no one in all-under-heaven to be his enemy — the highest wit of the Daoists.

The close: "what the ancients meant by 'the bent are made whole' — were those idle words? Wholeness truly comes home to him." The silk text's 幾語才 says: is this an empty saying? 誠全歸之 says: he who bends himself to follow things finds wholeness come home in the end. The Doctrine of the Mean: "sincerity is the way of heaven" — and Laozi's 誠全歸之 speaks the reality of the bent-made-whole. Confucian and Daoist were never two roads: different ways up, one arrival.

Wang Bi's 抱一, "cradle the One," against the silk text's 執一, "hold the One": holding is keeping fast, cradling is nourishing — different words, one point: keeping the Dao in purity, holding De entire, and by it serving the Way of Heaven and steering the governance of men. The shepherd (牧) rears and tends — he does not cow with majesty: that is the sage as shepherd of all-under-heaven.
en.英譯:
Bent, then whole (曲則金, 金 an error for 全). Crooked, then straight. Hollow, then full. Worn, then new. Little, then gain. Much, then bewilderment.

Hence the sage holds the One (執一), to shepherd all-under-heaven (為天下牧).

Not self-seeing (不自視), hence shining-forth (章); not self-displaying, hence clear (明); not self-boasting, hence merit; not self-exalting, hence enduring.

Only because he does not contend — no one can contend with him.

What the ancients meant by "the bent are made whole" — were those mere empty words (幾語才)? Wholeness truly comes home to him (誠金歸之, 金 again for 全).

校記:
本章帛書原文據甲本，甲殘之「不自視故章不自見也故明」「古之所胃曲全者幾語才」二句據乙本補；字從《集成》（2014）括號外原字。

- 曲則金：從甲本。「金」為「全」之錯字，《集成》以〈全〉正之；乙本作「曲則全」。王弼本同乙本。
- 枉則定：從甲本，「定」讀為「正」；乙本作「汪則正」，「汪」讀為「枉」。王弼本作「枉則直」。
- 洼則盈　敝則新：從甲本，「洼」讀為「窪」；乙本「敝」字作上敝下衣之「𧝬」，圖版、1980 釋文與高明實錄同。
- 是以聲人執一以為天下牧：從甲本，「聲」讀為「聖」；乙本「聖」作⿰耳口之「𦔻」。王弼本作「是以聖人抱一為天下式」，「執」作「抱」，「牧」作「式」。
- 不自視故章不自見也故明：從乙本。甲本作「不【自】視故明，不自見故章」，乙本作「不自視故章，不自見也故明」，二本「明」「章」互易，乙本次句有「也」字。甲本殘「自」字，二句從乙本，以免明、章錯出。《集成》讀「視」為「示」、「章」為「彰」。王弼本作「不自見故明，不自是故彰」。
- 弗矜故能長：甲乙同；王弼本作「不自矜故長」。
- 故莫能與之爭：甲乙同；王弼本作「故天下莫能與之爭」。
- 古之所胃曲全者幾語才：甲本「古」下殘，據乙本。甲本「語」字，原釋文直接釋出，《集成》審其左旁碎片非「言」旁，已剔除，改釋作「唔（語）」；其上一字尚存殘畫，原釋文據乙本補為「幾」，《集成》取消補文，改作☐。乙本「才」讀為「哉」。王弼本作「古之所謂曲則全者，豈虛言哉」。（《集成》肆·頁51·注90）
- 誠金歸之：從甲本，「金」亦「全」之錯字；乙本作「誠全歸之」。王弼本作「誠全而歸之」。
